article_lead.description: a hundred-patient example relating cholesterol, sex and binary disease records to fitted probabilities

new_bank_questions.title: A fitted cholesterol probability
new_bank_questions.body: The displayed logistic model has score -9.3203-0.1094 I(male)+1.5842 cholesterol. Find the fitted disease probability for a male at cholesterol 5.5 and compare with a female at the same value.
new_bank_questions.answer: The male score is -0.7166 and the inverse-logit probability is about 0.32814. The female score is -0.6072 and probability about 0.35270. Their conditional probability difference is about -0.02456; this does not determine the marginal sex difference.

new_bank_questions.title: Odds and causation in the cholesterol example
new_bank_questions.body: The fitted cholesterol slope is 1.5842. Explain what exp(1.5842) compares and why it does not prove that an intervention lowering cholesterol would change disease risk.
new_bank_questions.answer: At the same sex, a one-unit higher cholesterol value has fitted disease odds exp(1.5842), about 4.88 times as large. The data description does not establish random assignment, control all confounders or document a causal intervention; the coefficient is an adjusted association in the fitted model.
